summary: Edited finish.mjs and re-ran make.sh (v1.nbt kept). Cut the palette to white, grey, birch and sand plus one aqua accent. Added a stepped rooftop pavilion with its own thin plate, projecting quartz fins and frames on the north wall, and weathered concrete, deck and plinth. Check reports 0 floating blocks; stray orphan blocks fell from 46 to 15 (palm-frond tips only).
applied: 1. Visible age: salt-grime runs of light_gray_concrete on the lower walls, deck boards mixed with pale_oak_planks and stripped_birch_log, worn stone and polished_andesite in the plinth, sand drifted onto the deck
2. Fewer colour families: parasol, surfboard banners and flowering azalea moved from orange, cyan, red and purple to white, light blue and green only
3. Massing: added a third box, a rooftop pavilion with sea-view glazing, a dark clerestory band and its own overhanging quartz plate, for a stepped, shaped top
4. Wall relief: quartz fins projecting 1 block on the north upper wall, a deepslate ledge under the ribbon window, and fins with a lintel framing the tall lower window
5. Livelier textures: the weathering and mixed boards bring texture variety within the narrower palette
Stray blocks: trimmed palm-frond tips that touched the build on one face and added a connecting log so the diagonal palm trunks stay attached (orphans 46 to 15)
skipped: 6. Purpose obvious from shape: the beach cues are already present (jetty, steps to sand, loungers, parasol, surfboards, pool, palms), and extra signage would clutter a minimalist house
Reviewer name: 'Modern open-plan house on beach' already matches the brief, so no identity fix was needed
Remaining palette flags (grime blocks flagged as outliers; birch trim on birch deck): left as is, because the grime is meant to read as age and the birch trim sits on white walls
